# dlcore origin

dlcore is derived from [Vino](https://github.com/cameron1729/Vino) at commit `490aa8e13488c9dbf0c88cb80aa4676d525a50ef` (2026-09-21), directory `revdi/`. It is licensed GPL-2.0-or-later; some kernel-derived files (under `dlcore/vino/`) are GPL-2.0-only, as their per-file `SPDX-License-Identifier` headers say. It is now maintained as its own fork and is no longer refreshed from upstream.

| Directory | Derived from | Crate | Licence |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dlcore/` | `revdi/chimera` | `dlcore` | GPL-2.0-or-later (kernel-derived files GPL-2.0-only) |
| `kernel-shim/` | `revdi/kernel-shim` | `kernel-shim` (library name `kernel`) | GPL-2.0-or-later |
| `dlcore-usb/` | `revdi/vino-driver` | `dlcore-usb` | GPL-2.0-or-later |
| `LICENSES/` | `revdi/LICENSES` | none | licence texts |

`dlcore/vino/` holds the literal DL3 protocol, HDCP 2.2 AKE, encrypted control plane, dock profiles, and video codec from the in-kernel `drm/vino` driver; dlcore compiles it in userspace over libusb. The `kernel-shim` crate must stay named `kernel` because those verbatim files `use kernel::...`.

## Changes when the fork was declared

Behaviour and wire bytes are unchanged; the replay checksums of the engine's benchmark clips (Ridge, Ella, Navarro, with and without gamma) and every test were identical before and after.

- Renamed `vendor/vino` to `vendor/dlcore`, `vino-chimera` to `dlcore` and `vino-driver` to `dlcore-usb` (binary `vino-sniff` became `dlcore-sniff`; `chimera-prove` and `chimera-coldstart` keep their names). The directories `chimera/` and `vino-driver/` became `dlcore/` and `dlcore-usb/`.
- Removed the `revdi` feature and its optional `evdi` dependency (the unvendored Linux Revdi client), the `daemon` module and the `chimera` daemon binary, and the `revdi` module, with their tests. A macOS host never uses them.
- Removed `simd.rs`, the x86-64-only stand-in for the kernel's AVX2 path. It always returned `None`, so the scalar path it selected is the one that already ran; nothing referenced it on other targets.
- Added the `oracle` feature (off by default, never enabled by the engine): `kshim::rng::seed_rng(seed)` makes `kshim::rng::fill` a per-thread splitmix64 stream, so a reimplementation can be compared byte for byte. Without the feature `fill` is unchanged.
- The three crates are listed as members of the engine's cargo workspace so they can be built and tested with `-p` from `engine/`.

## Design notes

Notes 1-7 were found or measured on a Humanscale M/Connect 2 (`17e9:600f`, Ridge firmware 12.2.25) with two HP Z27k G3 monitors. Later notes below are source-review improvements; their measurement and hardware-validation status is stated separately.

1. **Parallel encode** - `dlcore/src/scanout.rs`: `strip_hashes` and the fresh-body pass of `HeadScanout::encode` run across cores through `par_for_each_mut` (the shared worker pool of patch 15; passes under 64 strips stay on the calling thread). Upstream's only SIMD path is x86-64, so on Apple Silicon a serial 4K keyframe took 96 ms; parallel it takes 12 ms. Output is byte-identical to serial `encode_strip` + `frame_records` across all 8100 strips of a 4K frame.
2. **EDID readiness gate** - `dlcore/src/edid_fetch.rs`: before the dock reports its downstream read complete, only the dock's own `NVT` placeholder EDID is discarded (`is_dock_placeholder`). This dock never sets the readiness bit, so upstream discarded both monitors' real `HPN` EDIDs and lit nothing.
3. **Downstream-change notice** - `dlcore/src/session.rs`: replies read by `send_control` and `send_control_echoing` go through `ControlSession::receive`, which records the dock's `id=0x03 sub=0x82` push; `take_downstream_change()` exposes it. The engine probes lit heads only after this notice on shared-EDID-handler docks, because probing them once a second kept both monitors in standby.
4. **Settle pass** - `dlcore/src/scanout.rs` (`HeadScanout::settle`, `touched`) and `dlcore/src/session.rs` (`ControlSession::settle`): every strip changed since the last settle is owed another `damage_frames` round once the surface has been still for 100 ms. The engine paces those retransmissions one refresh apart. A transmission the dock missed or placed in the other buffer while things moved can therefore not leave a stale box behind.
5. **Video bytes returned** - `ControlSession::present_rgb` returns the bytes it submitted so the engine can hold all heads together to 100 MB/s (Vino's measured DLM rate on this family). Unthrottled full-screen motion on two 4K heads reset the dock off the bus within minutes. The limit covers the video bytes presents report, not status polls, cursor/control traffic or USB protocol overhead.
6. **Three ring slots** - `dlcore/vino/profile.rs`: Ridge `dock_buffers: 3` and `FrameDelivery::new(3, 1, 3)` (upstream 2 and `(2, 1, 3)`); the pinned assertion in `api.rs` follows. Ridge's frame trailer already cycles three phases (`ring_phase`, `seq % 3`), and Vino's notes record the vendor filling slots 0/2/4 in equal thirds. Two keyframe presentations left one slot stale, seen as patches flickering on a still screen.
7. **Dirty hint** - `dlcore/src/scanout.rs` (`HeadScanout::plan_dirty`, `strip_hashes_within`, `strip_hash`) and `dlcore/src/session.rs` (`ControlSession::present_rgb_dirty`): when the caller knows which areas changed (ScreenCaptureKit's dirty rects), only strips meeting them are hashed. Full-surface hashing of a 4K frame for a ticking menu-bar item was the largest steady CPU cost. `plan` and `present_rgb` keep upstream behaviour.
8. **Borrow cached strip bodies** - `dlcore/src/scanout.rs`, `dlcore/src/kvino/kernel_tree/api.rs`, and `dlcore/vino/video/haar/records.rs`: frame packing accepts `AsRef<[u8]>` strip bodies and reads the cache by reference instead of cloning each body and then copying it again into a `KVec`. Existing owned-vector callers remain supported by the generic API; packing order, codec bytes, and record boundaries are unchanged. The structural reduction is two body allocations and two body copies per selected cached strip. Owned-versus-borrowed byte-equality regressions cover keyframes and damage across Ella/Ridge/Navarro, both depths and connector selectors.
9. **Pack directly into USB chunks** - `dlcore/src/session.rs`: `prefix_frame` fills the final 65536-byte transfers directly rather than building a complete contiguous stream and copying it into transfers. Part order, trailer phases, and exact chunk boundaries are unchanged; a hardware-free regression compares against the former concatenation algorithm at transfer-boundary cases on all three supported dock families. Eliminates one full-stream allocation/copy by construction; no runtime/RSS measurements or dock validation performed for this patch.
10. **Retain cancelled IN transfers until completion** - `dlcore-usb/src/usb.rs`: teardown no longer frees transfers, their buffers, or callback state after an arbitrary 500 ms when callbacks remain outstanding. It waits until every submitted transfer is returned, matching the existing OUT cleanup rule. A hardware-free regression uses a real allocated libusb transfer and the real cancellation callback delayed beyond 500 ms. Cleanup can wait indefinitely if libusb never returns a cancelled transfer; releasing callback-owned memory instead is not safe.
11. **Bound queued device replies** - `dlcore-usb/src/usb.rs`: retain at most 256 EP84 replies (at most 2 MiB of payload at the existing 8192-byte transfer size). A device flooding IN while OUT pumps events could previously grow the queue without bound. Overflow clears queued data, stops rearming completed IN transfers, and makes receive fail with the existing USB overflow error rather than silently dropping a push and continuing an out-of-sync session. Added hardware-free queue-order/capacity/fail-closed coverage. The limit is a defensive ceiling, not a measured legitimate high-water mark; hardware validation remains outstanding.
12. **Present stage timings** - `dlcore/src/session.rs` (`PresentTiming`, `ControlSession::last_present`) and `dlcore/src/scanout.rs` (`HeadScanout::last_plan_coarse`): `present_rgb_dirty` reads the clock around plan, encode, report/transfer packing, `submit_video` and the status poll, and records whether the plan was patch 13's coarse superset, for the engine's performance counters. The timings themselves change no call order, wire bytes or return values.
13. **Coarse delta instead of keyframe fallback** - `dlcore/src/scanout.rs` (`plan_dirty`, `coarse_owed_rects`): change too scattered for `MAX_RECTS` exact rectangles is planned as a delta of at most `MAX_RECTS` band rectangles covering every owing strip, presented once, instead of a keyframe presented `keyframe_presentations` (3) times back to back. This changes wire output for such frames: fewer presentations and bytes, the same record format. The retransmit debt still carries each changed strip to every dock buffer, and the settle pass is unchanged; the superset only resends strips the dock already holds. Measured on the M/Connect 2 with two HP Z27k G3 at 3840×2160@60 during App Exposé and desktop swipes (engine performance counters, busy seconds, median): head 0 went from 17 to 44 presents/s (worst second 14 → 30) and head 1 from 22 to 29 (11 → 18), with keyframe fallbacks 7/s → 0, USB time per present 20.9 → 11.2 ms and total video 66.5 → 47.6 MB/s; no dock reset or engine error was logged. Regression test: `scattered_change_is_a_coarse_delta_that_reaches_every_buffer`. `cargo test --locked -p dlcore` (28 tests) passes from `engine/`.
14. **Faster strip coder, same bytes** - `dlcore/vino/video/haar/transform.rs`, `dlcore/vino/video/haar/strip.rs`, `dlcore/src/kvino/kernel_tree/api.rs` (`encode_strip`, `RgbRows`): `Bits` appends each code as one word (`put`) instead of bit by bit and spills eight bytes at a time; `esc` is branch-free (a zero is the category-0 code). `colour_strip_at` codes each block as it is quantized (`StripCoder`) into one scratch buffer and allocates the exact body once, instead of collecting sixteen blocks (792 bytes each on 64-bit) in a heap vector and coding main/row0/row1 into three growing vectors; one block and one set of planes are reused per strip. Quantisation runs band by band with constant steps and finds the last significant coefficient branch-free. Pixels are read eight at a time through the new `PixelRows` trait (closures still work); `encode_strip`'s packed-RGB reader uses one range check and, on arm64, a NEON `ld3` per run. On arm64 with NEON (userspace only; the kernel's arm64 target has no NEON, so it keeps the scalar path) the Haar transform runs four lanes at a time, column pass first, which changes no coefficient because every step is an exact integer sum or difference. Wire output is byte-identical: the engine's 120-frame 4K scrolling-desktop benchmark keeps its checksum, and an old-vs-new differential build of `encode_strip` matched on 52,200 strips (Ella, Ridge and Navarro; 8-bit synthetic patterns including noise, extremes, gradients, chroma-only and block edges; a full 4K desktop at 8-bit and at 10-bit) with overflow checks on; `chimera-prove` passes. New tests compare the NEON transform and row reader with their scalar versions, and `esc`/significance/AC coding with a one-bit-at-a-time reference for both code tables at every accumulator alignment. Encode CPU on Apple M5 Pro fell from 21.4 to 7.9 ms per frame (medians of three). Hardware status: measured offline; no dock was attached.
15. **Persistent worker pool and lane-split strip hash** - `dlcore/src/pool.rs` (new), `dlcore/src/lib.rs`, `dlcore/src/scanout.rs` (`par_for_each_mut`, `strip_hash`, `StripHasher`): `par_for_each_mut` runs on a process-wide pool of `available_parallelism - 1` parked threads instead of spawning scoped threads per pass; the displaylink-lite engine uses the same pool for capture conversion and gamma, and `StripHasher` for its capture-side BGRA strip hash (`engine/src/host.rs`, `bgra_strip_hash`, still `| 1` so 0 means unknown). Callers always work through their own pass and idle workers join, so concurrent and nested callers cannot deadlock and a panic resumes in the caller after every worker has left. Memory-streaming passes (strip hashing) use at most `STREAMING_THREADS` (8) threads; encode uses all. `strip_hash` now feeds `StripHasher`, eight independent multiply-xor lanes over 64-byte steps folded at the end, instead of one serial chain; it is still position-seeded and only ever compared with itself, so plans and wire bytes are unchanged. Measured with a throwaway benchmark feeding 120 frames of a real 3840×2160 desktop scrolling diagonally through capture → plan → encode on an M5 Pro (median of 3, CPU ms per frame): plan 2.16 → 0.67, encode 21.5 → 19.3 (pool only; codec unchanged), with byte-identical output (same total bytes and checksum). Hardware-free tests cover pool coverage, concurrent nested callers and panic propagation, and the hasher noticing every single-byte flip and line swap. No dock was attached.
16. **Strips coded from supplied coefficients and hashes** - `dlcore/vino/video/haar/strip.rs` (`last_significant` becomes `pub(crate)`, nothing else), `dlcore/src/kvino/kernel_tree/api.rs` (`QuantBlock`, `quantize_strip`, `encode_strip_quantized`, `StripEncoding`, `CodeTable`, `STRIP_MAGIC`, `STRIP_BODY_MAX`, `DockProfile::strip_encoding`, `DockProfile::family`), `dlcore/src/scanout.rs` (`HeadScanout::plan_hashed`, `offer_bodies`, `encode_cached`, `CachedEncodeError`) and `dlcore/src/session.rs` (`ControlSession::present_encoded`, `PresentEncodedError`): the entry points a GPU strip encoder needs. The producer does the colour transform, Haar and quantiser and hands over `i16` coefficients, which `encode_strip_quantized` turns into `ColourBlock`s with lasts from the coder's own `last_significant` and codes through the unchanged `colour_strip`/`StripCoder`. Every quantised coefficient fits `i16` at 10 bits (magnitude at most 4092; derivation on `QuantBlock`). `quantize_strip` is the CPU reference for that stage. On the scanout side, `plan_hashed` takes the producer's strip hashes for the strips it reports changed, and `plan_dirty` shares the same reshape and debt/touched/owed-rect tail (`reshape`, `plan_pending`). `encode_cached` frames only already-current bodies and returns `MissingBody` instead of encoding. `encode` keeps its behaviour and shares the selection and framing helpers. `present_encoded` mirrors `present_rgb_dirty`, whose send/publish/poll tail is now the shared `send_planned`. Wire output of the existing paths is unchanged and every earlier test passes unmodified. New tests: `quantised_strips_code_to_the_bytes_encode_strip_produces` (Ella, Ridge and Navarro, 8 and 10 bits, flat, noise, extremes, gradients, chroma-only, block-edge and one-pixel-grating surfaces, every strip), `quantised_coefficients_stay_within_the_i16_bound`, `strip_encoding_states_each_docks_coder`, `a_strip_beyond_the_wire_coordinates_is_refused`, `supplied_hashes_and_bodies_put_the_same_records_on_the_wire` (both paths through damage, overlapping retransmit debt, settle, a cached keyframe and a resize, comparing plans and records on all three families at both depths) and `a_strip_without_a_current_body_is_named_not_framed`; `cargo test --locked -p dlcore` (41 tests) passes from `engine/`. The engine's encoded mailbox (`engine/src/host.rs`, `Shared::submit_encoded`) feeds `present_encoded`, and a `MissingBody` there asks the producer to code every strip again. The producer is the app's `MetalStripEncoder` (`Sources/LinkLiteGPU`), checked strip by strip against `quantize_strip` and `encode_strip` and end to end against the CPU feed's replay checksums. No dock was attached.
17. **Outputs and heads are separate** - `dlcore/vino/profile.rs` (`Topology::outputs`: Ridge 3, Ella 2, Navarro 4; the `connectors` doc now says heads), `dlcore/src/kvino/kernel_tree/api.rs` (`DockProfile::outputs`, `assign_head_req`, `reply_status`, `reply_status_ok`, `probe_reports_sink`), `dlcore/src/edid_fetch.rs` (`fetch_edid(output, heads)` returns the head it assigned, `Request`, `await_status`, `FetchError::NoHead`), `dlcore/src/session.rs` (`head_output` map, `output_count`, `head_output`, `output_head`, `has_free_head`, `release_head`; `fetch_edid` takes an output and returns `(head, edid)`; `probe_output_present` replaces `probe_head_present`) (the Linux daemon that also followed this API was removed later). The firmware addresses physical outputs and video heads separately; upstream used one number for both, which only holds where they coincide, as on the M/Connect 2. From static analysis of DisplayLink Manager 16.x: `id=0x16 sub=0x23` is `Output::assignHead` with the output at byte 22 and the head at byte 23 (`0xff` unassigns), `id=0x15 sub=0x53` is the cursor-capability query with a head bitmask at byte 22, and the reply status is the u16 at reply offset 20 (0 ok, `0x0b` tolerated, anything else an error). The presence probe, the readiness kick (`0x16/0x4b`) and the EDID read keep selecting the output. Measured on a Targus DOCK310 (`17e9:6024`, "RidgeDoc" 12.2.25, two heads, three outputs, HDMI on output 2, Dell U2713H): assigning output 2 to head 2 answers status 3, to head 0 `0x0d`, to head 1 0; with output 2 on head 1 and everything video-side (set-mode, markers, `strm2`, downstream authentication, endpoint `0x0b`, stream `0x09`) on head 1, the stock Ridge profile showed a picture at 2560x1440@60 and 1920x1080@60. The probe's status word reads `03 01 20 00` (output 0, empty), `05 01 60 00` (output 1, empty) and `04 01 27 00` (output 2, monitor), so bit `0x1000` never reports this HDMI sink; `probe_reports_sink` also accepts a word whose byte 24 has bits 1 and 2 both set (`0x27` with a sink on both docks; `0x20`, `0x21`, `0x60` and `0x61` empty), which adds nothing for any word the M/Connect 2 has reported empty. `ControlSession::fetch_edid` offers an output the head it already holds, else its own number when that head exists and is free, then the other free heads from the lowest. The first engage of the existing two is the trial: its status is read inside the step delay that already followed it, so a dock that accepts the first head is sent the same records with the same timing, a refused head is followed by an engage offering the next, and a status that does not arrive is taken as acceptance, as every engage was before. The engine (`engine/src/host.rs`) discovers, probes and detaches by output (`attach`, `refresh_topology`, the empty-socket scan) and keeps the head everywhere else; a head is released when its monitor is dropped or could not be lit, with nothing sent to the dock. On the M/Connect 2 the selector bytes of every EDID request are unchanged (`an_output_on_its_own_head_is_sent_the_upstream_records`, `assigning_an_output_to_its_own_head_is_the_upstream_engage`); what it does see that is new is a presence probe of output 2 while a head is still free (outputs without a head are not probed once every head is taken), and, only when nothing at all was found at engage, a blind fetch of output 2. Also pinned: `requests_select_the_output_or_the_head_they_address`, `presence_follows_the_measured_status_words`, `ridge_has_more_outputs_than_heads`. Untested on hardware: the DOCK310's DisplayPort output, two monitors on it at once, and whether a refused trial (`0x0d`) leaves anything behind. `cargo test --locked -p dlcore` (46 tests) passes from `engine/`. This code then ran on the same dock with no debug switches: `dllite-probe` placed output 2 on head 1 by itself (head 0 refused with `0x0d`), and the LinkLite app lit the Dell at 2560x1440@60 and held about 55 fps of motion through two benchmark runs with no resets.
18. **Opt-in protocol trace** - `dlcore/src/trace.rs` (new), `dlcore/src/lib.rs`, `dlcore/src/kvino/kernel_tree/api.rs` (`open_reply`), and call sites in `dlcore/src/session.rs` and `dlcore/src/edid_fetch.rs`. `DLL_TRACE=1` writes decrypted control replies (with the reply status and the probe status word named), mode-set plaintext, presence answers, each EDID request with its output and head, the status of every `0x23`, `0x4b` and `0x53` reply, and the HDCP pushes of each head's downstream authentication to stderr, folding repeats of a polling loop. It only reads bytes the session already holds, so the wire is the same with it unset.
19. **Transport seam** - `dlcore-usb/src/transport.rs` (new), `dlcore-usb/src/lib.rs`, `dlcore-usb/src/usb.rs` (constants made public, the 2000 ms default, 2 s completion deadline and 1000 ms identity timeout named), `dlcore/src/session.rs` and `dlcore/src/edid_fetch.rs`: the `Transport` trait holds exactly the `Dock` operations the session and the EDID fetch call (`connectors`, `vendor_in`, `vendor_out`, `std_in`, `std_out_iface`, `claim_interface`, `write_ctrl_raw`, `write_ctrl_dlm`, `write_video_frame`, `clear_video_halt`, `recv_frame_raw_timeout`), and `Dock` implements it by forwarding to its inherent methods. `ControlSession` holds a `Box<dyn Transport>`; `ControlSession::engage` is `engage_on` over `Dock::open`, so the libusb path runs the same calls in the same order with the same arguments, and `engage_on` lets a host bring its own transport (the macOS app's IOUSBHost one) under the same placement rule. A hardware-free test engages over a scripted transport and checks the exact call sequence up to the first awaited reply, and that a failed engage drops the transport.
20. **Host-replaceable session clock** - `dlcore/src/kshim.rs` (`kshim::clock`: `now`, `sleep`, `Instant`, and under `oracle` the `Clock` trait and `set_clock`), `dlcore/src/session.rs` and `dlcore/src/edid_fetch.rs`: every clock read and sleep on the session path goes through `kshim::clock` instead of `std::time::Instant::now` and `std::thread::sleep` (the activation bracket's anchor and paced waits, the carrier-frame and 120 ms blank deadlines with their 16 ms status polls, the probe-reply and per-head push drains, the H' wait, the video-engine commit pauses, the present stage timings, and the EDID fetch's step, poll and wall-time bounds). Without the `oracle` feature `clock::Instant` is `std::time::Instant` and `now`/`sleep` are the std calls, so the code compiles to what it was. With `oracle` and no clock installed, readings are the same `std::time::Instant` source held as an offset from a process-wide origin, and sleeps are `std::thread::sleep`. With `oracle`, `clock::set_clock(Some(..))` installs a host clock for the calling thread only, like `rng::seed_rng`; the swiftlink oracle exposes it as `slo_set_clock`. Why: those loops decide how many transport calls the session makes from what the clock says, so a recorded hardware session could only be replayed byte for byte up to scheduling jitter (a 424 MB Targus DV4K recording matched 17,884 of 17,885 session calls and then diverged inside the blank's deadline loop). A trace now records every reading and replay serves them back. Not routed: `kshim::Instant<Monotonic>` (the kernel codec's own phase timing, which decides nothing), and the timeouts inside `dlcore-usb`'s libusb `Dock` (`usb.rs`: receive wait, DLM completion deadline, video pipeline grace). Those run inside a transport call, and only the call's outcome reaches the session, which a trace records anyway; a host transport replaces them entirely. Hardware-free tests: `kshim::clock::tests` (per-thread install, no real sleeping, std-equivalent arithmetic) and `session::tests::a_host_clock_decides_the_blank_and_nothing_else_does` (the blank's frame count follows the host clock alone and repeats exactly for the same readings, with no real time spent). `cargo test --locked -p dlcore --features oracle` (53 tests) and `-p dlcore -p dlcore-usb` (48 + 8) pass from `engine/`; `chimera-prove` passes. No dock was attached; a recording with clock readings from a dock is still needed to confirm the replay closes the observed divergence.

Hardware-free checks passed for patches 8-11: `cargo test --locked -p dlcore` (27 tests) and `cargo test --locked -p dlcore-usb` (8 tests), from `engine/`; the root engine dependency enables `live`. A temporary optimized-build benchmark packed the same patterned 3840×2160 Ridge frame 50 times: the former copying path took 204.1 ms, borrowed packing 119.2 ms. Each frame avoids 16,200 strip-body allocations and 41,988,360 copied body bytes by construction. This is a packing microbenchmark, not a full rendering benchmark or a process-RSS measurement; no dock was attached. The temporary benchmark was removed after measurement.

Tried and reverted (measured worse on this dock): a zero-length packet after full-packet frames (did not stop resets), presenting each delta twice (`FrameDelivery::new(2, 2, 3)`; doubled bandwidth and reset the dock without the rate limit).

The numbered items are the changes made on top of the Vino source before the fork was declared; paths and crate names are the current ones.

Build the crates through `engine/` (`cargo test --locked -p dlcore -p dlcore-usb`); the engine manifest carries the `libusb1-sys` patch they need.
